Hi Hiro — thanks for the quick note and for sending the samples. A few items from procurement side to keep the onboarding moving:

1) Invoice content: please include Consumption Tax as a separate line with the tax rate and amount (消費税 10%: JPY X,XXX). We need a clear tax line for accounting and VAT/consumption-tax reporting.

2) Registration numbers: please place your 法人番号 (13-digit corporate number) on the invoice and attach a scanned copy of the 登記事項証明書. That will confirm domestic registration and lets us treat the vendor as a Japan-registered supplier.

3) Billing entity: confirm which legal entity you will invoice (Sakura Logistics KK — Japan, or Sakura Logistics Ltd. — overseas). If you invoice Redwood KK (our Japan entity) then domestic rules apply and we generally do not withhold consumption tax. If you invoice Redwood, Inc. (US) or another non-JP Redwood entity, Finance may need to evaluate withholding.

4) Bank details / tax residency: please include bank routing details and state whether your invoice is for goods delivered in Japan or for services (e.g., consultancy, warehousing). The nature of the supply affects withholding and tax treatment.

I attached a short checklist we use for Japan vendor onboarding to make sure we have everything (redwood_jp-vendor-tax-checklist.pdf).

If it's easier, Laura from Finance (cc'd) can confirm whether any withholding would apply if you bill a non-JP Redwood entity.

Next steps for you: attach the 登記事項証明書 and an invoice showing the Consumption Tax line, confirm billing entity and supply type. Once we have that we'll push the record through the vendor portal and kick off PO matching.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-minute call if helpful.

Best,

Hi Hiro / Jonas — looping in Finance to confirm treatment. Short summary from accounting: 

- If Sakura is a Japan-registered corporation (法人番号 present on invoice) and you invoice Redwood KK (our Japan entity), treat the invoice as domestic supply. Consumption Tax should be shown as a separate line and will be processed per domestic tax rules. No withholding at source for domestic-supply invoices.

- If Sakura is a foreign entity (no 法人番号) and invoices a non-JP Redwood entity, we may need to review withholding tax obligations depending on the service type and payment origin. For example, certain cross-border service fees can be subject to withholding under Japanese law when paid from Japan; conversely, if payment originates from Redwood US, US tax rules apply. We will confirm once we see the billing entity and payment route.

Requested documents for AP to set up the vendor and avoid payment delays:
- Scanned 登記事項証明書 (corporate certificate) or equivalent tax registration proof
- Sample invoice with Consumption Tax broken out (as Jonas requested)
- Confirmation of billing entity (company legal name and address)
- Bank account details and whether the account is JP-local (zengin) or offshore

Please upload the documents to the vendor portal link below or reply to this thread with attachments. Once AP has the docs we'll create the vendor record and align the PO.

Vendor portal: https://redwood.app/vendor-portal/RWI-7893

If you'd like, we can schedule a quick call tomorrow morning JST to walk through the checklist and confirm the correct invoice flow.
